newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA INDUSTRY, MINES FACE TOUGHER "GREEN" LAWS.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA INDUSTRY, MINES FACE TOUGHER "GREEN" LAWS.

text.p: South African Environment Minister Pallo Jordan on Tuesday invited public comment on his plans to clean up the country's environment, which include tougher measures for mines and industry.

A statement from Jordan set August 29 as the deadline for comment on his white paper on environmental management, which has been approved by the cabinet and was published in the government gazette at the end of last month.
Jordan's spokeswoman Cassandra Gabriel told reporters key elements of the white paper included rejection of the idea that industry could police itself on pollution issues.
"An integrated and comprehensive regulatory system is proposed to ensure compliance and cooperation," she said.
"The environment is no longer an afterthought but an integral part of the development of our country."

Gabriel noted that the new policy was underpinned by the "cradle to grave" philosophy under which responsibility for a product which was potentially hazardous to the environment would remain with the manufacturer up to and including safe disposal.

On environmental impact studies, Jordan's document commits the government to "a risk averse and cautious approach that recognises the limits of current knowledge about the environmental consequences of decisions or actions".
